newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt up after mixed German economic data.
newsitem.headline: German debt up after mixed German economic data.

text.p: German government bonds were higher in late trade on Thursday after a pair of economic indicators here painted a mixed picture of the economy.
German GDP, which posted 1.5 percent quarter-on-quarter growth, suggested that the economy may be growing more strongly than thought, pushing Bunds slightly lower.
The figure was quickly followed up by a rise in German unemployment which some traders said carried more weight in the market as it was more recently compiled.
In late afternoon trade, the September Bund future was up 20 basis points at 97.47, but off its high of 97.54.
Traders said Bunds got a lift from the GDP data because market talk late on Wednesday had been for growth over two percent.
"People were a little relieved even though the GDP figure came in close to what economists had expected," said one trader at a major German bank in Frankfurt.

Bunds strongly outperformed T-notes after the release after the release of U.S. jobless claims, pushing the yield spread out to minus 71 basis points, near the highest spread in weeks, from minus 64 basis points earlier in the day.
Bunds also got a lift from stronger markets elsewhere in Europe.
Traders said the September Bund future should trade in a range between 97.30 and 97.60 until the release of U.S. unemployment data on Friday at 1230 GMT.

Traders said Bunds may be able to outperform T-notes if the the jobs data comes in strong, dragging down debt markets. Bunds would underperform on the other hand if the jobs data shows a weak U.S. economy and lifts Treasuries.
